historical_references.reference: Azadeh, meaning 'free from sorrow,' is a name given to the heroine of the Persian epic poem, Khosrow and Shirin, written by the poet Nezami Ganjavi around 1197 CE. The story portrays the tragic love story between Shah Khosrow and Shirin, whose love is forbidden due to a prior promise made by the king.

The name Azadeh is also given to a character in The Conference of the Birds by the Persian poet Fariduddin Attar, written around 1177 CE. According to the story, Azadeh represents 'joy and delight' and is one of the 'forty wise men from the land of Simorgh,' who embark on a journey to find the Simorgh, the king of birds.
